prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” broker for everyone — the right broker depends on what kind of coverage you need (individual/family, small‑group/employer, Medicare, Medicaid/CHIP), your budget, whether you want lots of hand‑holding, and whether you prefer an independent agent or one aligned with a particular carrier.

I can help you find a good broker, but first some quick, practical guidance and a short checklist to pick a strong local broker in Kansas City:

How to find a good Kansas City broker
- Decide the coverage type (individual/ACA, small business, Medicare Advantage/Part D, etc.). Brokers often specialize.
- Use reputable sources: Kansas Insurance Department (to verify licensing/complaints), Healthcare.gov (for assister/navigator contacts for ACA), Medicare.gov (for Medicare agents), and the National Association of Health Underwriters (NAHU) “Find an Agent” tool.
- Look for independent agents who represent multiple carriers if you want comparison shopping; captive agents represent a single carrier.
- Check online reviews (Google, Yelp) and ask friends/family or your HR/payroll contact for referrals.

Questions to ask any broker before you hire them
- Are you licensed in Kansas (and Missouri if you need cross‑state coverage)? Can you provide your license number?
- Do you work independently or for a particular carrier? Which carriers do you represent?
- How are you paid — commission from the insurer, or do you charge a fee? (Get this in writing.)
- Do you have experience with my specific needs (ACA subsidies, small-group plans, Medicare, chronic conditions)?
- Will you help with enrollment, plan comparisons, appeals/claims, and renewals? What is ongoing support like?
- Can you provide references from clients in Kansas City?
- Will you provide a written plan summary and all fees/commissions in writing?

Where to look right now
- Kansas Insurance Department website — verify licenses and complaints.
- Healthcare.gov local assister navigator directory (if you’re applying for ACA Marketplace plans).
- Medicare.gov agent/broker finder (for Medicare).
- NAHU “Find an Agent” (national directory).
- Local community health centers and consumer assistance programs often have recommendations for trustworthy brokers or certified navigators.

If you want, I can:
- Look up licensed brokers/agencies near you if you give your ZIP code and the type of plan you need (individual, family, small business, Medicare).
- Draft an email or script you can use when contacting brokers with the right questions.

Which kind of plan are you shopping for, and what is your ZIP code?
